record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a function f such that every finite connected geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane, with straight-line edges carrying positive integer multiplicities, allowing edge intersections and self-intersections, satisfying the multiplicity-weighted balancing condition at each balanced vertex, and having n unbalanced vertices, diameter D, and total length L counted with multiplicity, has fewer than f(L/D, n) balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.4.2. There exists a function f of such that each geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane with n unbalanced vertices, diameter D, and total length L has less than f (L/D, n) balanced vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a finite connected graph $G=(V,E)$ together with an embedding (allowing edge crossings and self-intersections) such that:
- each edge $e\in E$ is realized as a straight line segment between its two endpoints in $\mathbb{R}^2$;
- each edge $e$ carries a positive integer multiplicity $m(e)\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.

For a vertex $v\in V$, let $E(v)$ denote the set of edges incident to $v$, and for $e\in E(v)$ let $\mathbf{u}_{v,e}\in\mathbb{R}^2$ be the unit vector at $v$ pointing along $e$ away from $v$. A vertex $v$ is called balanced if
$$\sum_{e\in E(v)} m(e)\,\mathbf{u}_{v,e}=\mathbf{0},$$
and unbalanced otherwise.

The total length counted with multiplicity is $L=\sum_{e\in E} m(e)\cdot\mathrm{length}(e)$, and the diameter $D$ is the diameter of the vertex set (or of the union of edges) of the multinet in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Question: Does there exist a function $f:\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for every finite connected geodesic multinet in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $n$ unbalanced vertices, diameter $D>0$, and total length $L$, the number of balanced vertices is strictly less than $f(L/D,\,n)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open. Recent work (e.g., a 2024 result showing at most one balanced vertex for three boundary vertices, and 2025 constructions producing irreducible geodesic nets with 4 unbalanced vertices and up to 25 balanced vertices) continues to investigate bounds on balanced vertices in terms of boundary data, but no proof of the full length/diameter bound $f(L/D,n)$ has been established.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 1.6 states that there exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with 4 unbalanced vertices and an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices... irreducible geodesic net with 4 boundary vertices and 25 balanced vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on bounds for balanced vertices continues; full conjecture not resolved.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: For three boundary vertices, there can be at most one single balanced vertex.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results known in special cases but not the general length-diameter bound.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open conjecture about a bound f(L/D, n) on balanced vertices.
